(sec-item-objectcontactconecone)=
# ObjectContactConeCone

A penalty contact between two truncated cones, each centered at its marker along the local z axis of the marker, with their sides, caps and rims (a radius 0 gives a pointed cone, equal radii a cylinder); up to 4 contact points carry a line or a face of contact. Contact law and friction as for ObjectContactSphereTriangle.

Author: Gerstmayr Johannes

**Simpler**: [`mbs.CreateConeConeContact`](#sec-mainsystemextensions-createconeconecontact) adds this item, with what it needs, in one call.

## Interface

- Nodes it takes: [](#sec-item-nodegenericdata)
- Markers it acts on: those providing `Position` and `Orientation`: [](#sec-item-markerbodyrigid), [](#sec-item-markernoderigid), [](#sec-item-markersuperelementrigid), [](#sec-item-markerkinematictreerigid), [](#sec-item-markerbodyuser)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'ContactConeCone':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | connector's unique name |
| **markerNumbers** | ArrayMarkerIndex | 2 | [ invalid (-1), invalid (-1) ] | (symbol: $[m0,m1]\tp$) list of markers: the centers of cone 0 and cone 1, the local z axis of each marker the axis of its cone |
| **nodeNumber** | NodeIndex |  | invalid (-1) | (symbol: $n_d$) node number of a NodeGenericData with numberOfDataCoordinates = 12 (24 with isHollowCone1), needed for the discontinuous iteration (friction and contact): a block of 3 for each of the up to 4 (8) contact points $i$ holds the values of the last PostNewton iteration: data[3i] the gap, data[3i+1] the norm of the tangential velocity (stick or slip), data[3i+2] the impact velocity; with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 a block of 4, the fourth the plastic overlap |
| **conesRadii0** | Vector2D | 2 | [0.,0.] | (symbol: $[r_{0,0},r_{0,1}]\tp$) the radii of cone 0 at $z=-L_0/2$ and at $z=L_0/2$ along the local z axis of marker 0, >= 0 and not both 0 [SI:m] |
| **conesRadii1** | Vector2D | 2 | [0.,0.] | (symbol: $[r_{1,0},r_{1,1}]\tp$) the radii of cone 1 at $z=-L_1/2$ and at $z=L_1/2$ along the local z axis of marker 1, >= 0 and not both 0 [SI:m] |
| **conesLengths** | Vector2D | 2 | [0.,0.] | (symbol: $[L_0,L_1]\tp$) the lengths of cone 0 and cone 1 along the local z axes of their markers, both > 0 [SI:m] |
| **isHollowCone1** | Bool |  | False | if True, cone 1 is hollow, a bore or a seat with its radii and its length, open at both ends, and cone 0 is inside it: the contact is with the inner wall of cone 1 (#3334); then the data node needs 24 coordinates; checked at Assemble: the radius of cone 0 not larger than that of cone 1 |
| **dynamicFriction** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\mu_d$) dynamic friction coefficient for friction model, see StribeckFunction in exudyn.physics, [](#sec-module-physics) |
| **frictionProportionalZone** | UReal |  | 0.001 | (symbol: $v_{reg}$) limit velocity [m/s] up to which the friction is proportional to velocity (for regularization / avoid numerical oscillations), see StribeckFunction in exudyn.physics (named regVel there!), [](#sec-module-physics) |
| **contactStiffness** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $k_c$) normal contact stiffness [SI:N/m] (units in case that $n_\mathrm{exp}=1$) |
| **contactDamping** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $d_c$) linear normal contact damping [SI:N/(m s)]; this damping should be used (!=0) if the restitution coefficient is < 1, as it changes its behavior. |
| **contactStiffnessExponent** | PReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $n_\mathrm{exp}$) exponent in normal contact model [SI:1] |
| **contactPlasticityRatio** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\lambda_\mathrm{P}$) ratio of contact stiffness for first loading and unloading/reloading [SI:1] of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model, as in ObjectContactSphereSphere, with impactModel Linear: unloading and reloading with $K_2 = k_c/(1-\lambda_\mathrm{P})$ from the plastic overlap $\lambda_\mathrm{P}\,\delta_{max}$ of the contact; 0: the elastic law; not 0: each contact point has a block of 4 data coordinates, the fourth the plastic overlap (#3336) |
| **adhesionCoefficient** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $k_\mathrm{adh}$) coefficient for adhesion [SI:N/m] (units in case that $n_\mathrm{adh}=1$) of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model; used with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 |
| **adhesionExponent** | UReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $n_\mathrm{adh}$) exponent for adhesion coefficient [SI:1] of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model |
| **constantPullOffForce** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $f_\mathrm{adh}$) constant adhesion force [SI:N] of each contact point in contact, of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model; used with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 |
| **restitutionCoefficient** | PReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $e_\mathrm{res}$) coefficient of restitution [SI:1]; used in particular for impact mechanics; different models available within parameter impactModel; the coefficient must be > 0, but can become arbitrarily small to emulate plastic impact (however very small values may lead to numerical problems) |
| **minimumImpactVelocity** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\dot\delta_\mathrm{-,min}$) minimal impact velocity for coefficient of restitution [SI:1]; this value adds a lower bound for impact velocities for calculation of viscous impact force; it can be used to apply a larger damping behavior for low impact velocities (or permanent contact) |
| **impactModel** | ContactImpactModel |  | ContactImpactModel.Linear | (symbol: $m_\mathrm{impact}$) the impact model, see ContactImpactModel: Linear (only the linear contactDamping), HuntCrossley or GonthierCarvalhoMartins, the latter much more accurate regarding the coefficient of restitution in the full range (0, 1]; the integers 0, 1, 2 are accepted as well; in all models, the linear contactDamping is added, if not set to zero (#3327) |
| **activeConnector** | Bool |  | True | flag, which determines, if the connector is active; used to deactivate (temporarily) a connector or constraint |
| **contactForceUserFunction** | ObjectContactConeConeContactForceUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\mathrm{UF} \in \Rcal^3$) A Python function which replaces the contact law and returns the contact force on marker 0, while the item computes the geometry and the contact state; the contact parameters of the item are then not used; see description below (#3324) |
| **visualization** | VObjectContactConeCone |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all connectors](#sec-drawing-objectsconnector); both truncated cones with `contact.show.cones`; with `contact.showContactForces`, the force of each contact point on marker 0 as a red and on marker 1 as a green arrow, meeting at the point (#3339).

Settings beyond those of all connectors: [`contact.color.cones`](#sec-vsettingscontactcolor), [`contact.contactForcesFactor`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`contact.contactForcesRadius`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`contact.show.cones`](#sec-vsettingscontactshow), [`contact.showContactForces`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`general.cylinderTiling`](#sec-vsettingsgeneral).

## Output variables

Available as `OutputVariableType` in sensors, `Get...Output()` and other functions:

```{tabularcolumns} \Y{0.25}\Y{0.25}\Y{0.5}
```

| output variable | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| Distance |  | the signed distance of the two cones, the gap (< 0: penetration), from the current configuration, also with activeConnector = False |
| Position |  | the center of the contact points weighted by their normal forces; without contact force the middle of the closest points |
| Displacement |  | global vector from the closest point of cone 0 to that of cone 1 |
| Velocity |  | velocity of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0 at Position |
| DisplacementLocal |  | 1D Vector, containing only gap |
| Director1 |  | the contact normal, the unit vector from cone 0 towards cone 1 |
| Force |  | global contact force on marker 0, the sum of the contact points; marker 1 gets its negative |
| Torque |  | global torque of the contact forces on marker 0, about its position |

(description-objectcontactconecone)=
## Detailed description

### Definition of quantities

| intermediate variables | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| marker m0, m1 positions | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m1}$ | the centers of the cones |
| marker m0, m1 orientations | $\LU{0,m0}{\Rot}$, $\LU{0,m1}{\Rot}$ | the rotations of the cones, each axis the local z axis of its marker |
| marker velocities | $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m1}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m1}$ | global velocities and angular velocities |
| data coordinates | $\xv=[x_0,\,\ldots,\,x_{11}]\tp$ | for contact point $i$: the gap ($3i$), the norm of the tangential velocity ($3i+1$), the impact velocity ($3i+2$) |

### Geometric relations

Cone $i$ has the radii $r_{i,0}$ at $z=-L_i/2$ and $r_{i,1}$ at $z=L_i/2$ in the frame of marker $i$ and the length
$L_i$. Their signed distance $g$ - the output Distance -, the closest points - the deepest points of a penetration
- and the unit normal $\LU{0}{\nv}$ from cone 0 to cone 1 are computed by GJK and, for a penetration, EPA with a
refinement for the curved sides, the functions of `exudyn.cUtilities.Distance` with shapes of the type Cone.

A line or a face of contact is carried by up to 4 contact points $k$, each with its gap $g_k$, its normal
$\LU{0}{\nv}_k$ and its points on both cones:

- **on a cap**, where the normal is along an axis: the other cone against the cap as a face, by the points
described for ObjectContactCylinderTriangle with the radii of the rims, clipped to the disc of the cap;
- **on the side**, in penetration: the side line of cone 0 through its closest point - from its rim at $z=-L_0/2$
to its rim at $z=L_0/2$ in the same half-plane through the axis -, with the signed distance of its points to
cone 1, a convex function along the line: the two ends of the interval where it penetrates (by bisection) and
the closest point, which carries only the penetration beyond the line between the ends. Cones rolling on each
other along a side line, as bevel gears, rest on the two ends; crossing cones on the closest point.
- otherwise the closest points of GJK and EPA, one point.

The contact point is the middle of the points on both cones, and the relative velocity there is that of the body
of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0.

With `isHollowCone1 = True`, cone 1 is hollow - a bore or a seat, open at both ends, its wall at the radii of
cone 1 - and cone 0 is inside it. On each rim of cone 0 - where cone 0 leaves the hollow
cone, the rim at its end plane - the point farthest from the axis of cone 1, in the direction of the
eccentricity of the rim, and the points at $\pm 120$ degrees on the rim are contact points, so that a centered
cone rests on all sides; for a centered rim the direction goes over into the local x axis of marker 0. The gap
of a point at the distance $\rho$ from the axis and the radius $R$ of the wall at its axial position is
$g = (R - \rho)/\sqrt{1 + R'^2}$, normal to the wall with the slope $R'$ of the radius; the normal is that of the
wall, outwards. The outer side of a rim within the hollow shape carries the contact, as the distance of a point of
a side line from the axis of cone 1 is largest at its ends.

### Connector forces

For each contact point, the normal force - from the penetration $\delta_k = -g_k$, with `contactStiffness`
$k_c$, the exponent $n_\mathrm{exp}$, `contactDamping` $d_c$ and the impact model `impactModel` with the
restitution coefficient - and the regularized dry friction with $\mu_d$ and `frictionProportionalZone` are
computed as for `ObjectContactSphereSphere`, see [](#sec-item-objectcontactspheresphere), with the normal
$\LU{0}{\nv}_k$ and the relative velocity at the contact point; the stiffness is that of each point, so a
line contact on two points is twice as stiff as a point contact. The force $\LU{0}{\fv}_k$ acts on marker 0
at the contact point, with the torque $(\LU{0}{\pv}_{c,k} - \LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}) \times \LU{0}{\fv}_k$, and
$-\LU{0}{\fv}_k$ on marker 1; the outputs Force and Torque are their sums on marker 0. The data coordinates of
each point hold its gap, tangential velocity and impact velocity of the last post Newton step, which decide on
contact and on the friction regime during the Newton iterations (active set).

**Userfunction**: `contactForceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, gap, gap_t, normal, tangentialVelocity, impactVelocity)`
A user function which replaces the contact law: it computes the contact force from the gap, its rate, the
contact normal, the tangential relative velocity and the impact velocity, while the item computes the geometry and
the contact state (#3324). It is called for each contact point in contact, as its block of the data node from the
last post Newton step says, and returns the force of that point.
The force is the one on marker 0 at the contact point, the convention of the output variable Force; marker 1 gets
its negative. A penetration $\delta = -g$ pushes marker 0 against the normal: the normal force $f_N > 0$ gives
$-f_N\, \nv$; a friction force on marker 0 acts along the tangential velocity.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs in which underlying item is defined |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs, allowing easy access to all object data via mbs.GetObjectParameter(itemNumber, ...) |
| `gap` | Real | $g$, the signed gap, negative in contact |
| `gap_t` | Real | $\dot g$, its rate: the relative velocity along the normal, negative while approaching |
| `normal` | Vector3D | $\LU{0}{\nv}$, the unit contact normal from marker 0 towards marker 1 (the output Director1) |
| `tangentialVelocity` | Vector3D | $\LU{0}{\vv}_t$, the velocity of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0 at the contact point, normal to $\LU{0}{\nv}$ |
| `impactVelocity` | Real | the velocity of approach at the last impact, from the data node, for impact models |
| **return value** | Vector3D | the global contact force on marker 0, a list or numpy array of 3 values |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

*Example*:

```python
#the linear contact law with regularized friction as a user function: the same as contactStiffness, contactDamping,
#dynamicFriction and frictionProportionalZone of the item
def UFcontact(mbs, t, itemNumber, gap, gap_t, normal, tangentialVelocity, impactVelocity):
    k, d, mu, vReg = 1e5, 1e3, 0.3, 1e-3
    fN = -k*gap - d*gap_t                       #normal force, > 0 in compression
    vt = tangentialVelocity
    vtNorm = (vt[0]**2 + vt[1]**2 + vt[2]**2)**0.5
    fT = mu*fN/max(vtNorm, vReg)                #regularized Coulomb friction
    return [-fN*normal[i] + fT*vt[i] for i in range(3)]

mbs.AddObject(ObjectContactConeCone(markerNumbers=[mCone, mFixed], nodeNumber=nData, conesRadii0=[0.1,0.05],
              conesRadii1=[0.3,0.2], conesLengths=[0.2,0.2], contactForceUserFunction=UFcontact))
```

(miniexample-objectcontactconecone)=
## Mini example


```python
#a truncated cone standing on its larger cap on a fixed truncated cone
inertia = InertiaCylinder(density=1000, length=0.2, outerRadius=0.1, axis=2) #about that of the cone, for the example
node = mbs.AddNode(NodeRigidBodyEP(referenceCoordinates=[0,0,0.21]+eulerParameters0))
cone = mbs.AddObject(ObjectRigidBody(nodeNumber=node, mass=inertia.Mass(), inertia=inertia.GetInertia6D()))
mbs.AddLoad(LoadMassProportional(markerNumber=mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyMass(bodyNumber=cone)), loadVector=[0,0,-9.81]))
mCone = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=cone, localPosition=[0,0,0]))
mFixed = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=oGround, localPosition=[0,0,0]))
nData = mbs.AddNode(NodeGenericData(numberOfDataCoordinates=12, initialCoordinates=[0]*12))
mbs.AddObject(ObjectContactConeCone(markerNumbers=[mCone, mFixed], nodeNumber=nData, conesRadii0=[0.1,0.05],
                                    conesRadii1=[0.3,0.2], conesLengths=[0.2,0.2], contactStiffness=1e5, contactDamping=1e3))

mbs.Assemble()
simulationSettings = exu.SimulationSettings()
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.numberOfSteps = 1000
mbs.SolveDynamic(simulationSettings)

#at rest on 3 points of its rim: 0.1 + 0.1 - m*g/(3*k)
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetNodeOutput(node, exu.OutputVariableType.Position)[2]
```
